_comment: MLA prefill shapes for gfx950. seqlen_q = seqlen_k (full causal prefill). Covers DeepSeek V2/V3/V3.1/R1 (Hq=128) and Kimi-K2 (Hq=64). Canonical MLA geometry: qk_nope=128, qk_rope=64, v_head_dim=128, kv_lora_rank=512, q_lora_rank=1536, Hkv=1. block_size=16. fp8 variants included for the Phase 2 fp8 bench (gfx950+ only; see DESIGN.md S6 dtype plan).
_dtype_note: The fp8_e4m3 entries are Phase 2 (see DESIGN.md S6 dtype plan); Phase 1 is bf16 only. The existing prefill harnesses (benchmark_prefill2d_live.py, both arches) do not read this field at all: they load ndjson UAShape records via _ua_shape_utils.load_shapes and key dtype off the torch dtype strings q_dtype/k_dtype, with is_fp8 = ('float8' in shape.k_dtype); filter_prefill_2d drops non-bf16/fp16 shapes rather than defaulting them. This 'dtype' key is metadata for a future MLA runner. Do NOT run the fp8 entries against a bf16/fp16 harness and read the result as an fp8 number.
_harness_note: These shapes are a specification for a future MLA runner, not runnable input for the current one. The existing prefill harness loads ndjson UAShape records via _ua_shape_utils.load_shapes, not this nested-object JSON, so it parses zero shapes from this file and does so silently (undecodable lines are skipped). It also requires a per-shape 'head_size', which MLA has no single value for: d_nope+d_rope=192 for the score, d_V=128 for the output. Wiring MLA shapes into a runner is part of the kernel deliverable (DESIGN.md S9).
_batch_note: The batch axis here is deliberately narrower than the decode files' B in {1,4,8,32}, and it is measuring a different thing. Decode needs batch because the pre-step is batch-invariant while the flash loop is not, so the two crossovers of DESIGN.md S4 only appear across B. Prefill has no such crossover: its pre-kernel amortizes over total_q = batch * seqlen_q, so batch and seqlen_q are interchangeable for it and a uniform-length batch sweep re-measures points the seqlen sweep already covers, at multiplied cost. What batch does buy at prefill is coverage of the packed-varlen path -- cu_seqlens_q/cu_seqlens_k prefix sums and the per-sequence causal mask -- which B=1 exercises only trivially. Hence B=4 at the two short lengths, where that coverage is cheapest, and B=1 above. The batched entries are bf16 only: fp8 is Phase 2, and crossing the two axes would double a set that is already specification rather than runnable input. Mixed sequence lengths within a batch are the case that most needs covering and this schema cannot express them; that belongs with the runner work (DESIGN.md S9).

models._note: Hq=64 (differs from DeepSeek Hq=128); all other MLA geometry is identical.
